title: Structural Determination of Subviral Particles of Hepatitis B Virus using Cryo-Electron Microscopy and Cryo-Electron Tomography
content: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major global health threat, leading to significant morbidity and mortality from liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma [1, 2]. HBV exists in three morphological forms: ∼42-nm infectious Dane particles, and non-infectious filamentous and spherical subviral particles (SVPs) (Fig. 1A) [3]. SVPs outnumber infectious HBV virions by more than 10,000-fold and are believed to function as decoys, promoting immune tolerance and supporting the long-term persistence of chronic HBV infection [4]. Additionally, studying SVPs provides valuable insights into the distribution of antigens and morphological features present on infectious Dane particles.
